control.title: Services are processed in stages by independent parties such that there is segregation of duties from inception to completion

part.name: objective
part.p: Services are processed in stages by independent parties such that there is segregation of duties from inception to completion.

part.name: item
part.p: Appropriate segregation of duties is implemented for transaction processing through logical and/or physical access controls.

part.name: item
part.p: Access to record, authority to post and authorise transactions or services is restricted. Only authorised users have access to update customer service records.

control.title: Sample Controls for Data Entry Services

part.name: objective
part.p: Data entry procedures are performed in an accurate and timely manner.

part.name: applicability
part.p: Note: The following controls apply to data entry service providers only. Add this section if it is relevant to the service provided to the FIs.

part.name: item
part.p: Input forms are stamped with the date/time of receipt.

part.name: item
part.p: Input forms are batched and batch totals (e.g. number of forms are calculated and logged).

part.name: item
part.p: Batch totals are re-calculated upon data entry and reconciled with the log. Discrepancies are investigated and remediated.

part.name: item
part.p: Processed input forms are clearly marked to prevent re-input.

part.name: item
part.p: Keyed data are verified against the original input forms to verify accuracy of data entry.

part.name: item
part.p: The identities of the maker and checker are recorded for accountability.

control.title: Sample Controls for Debt Collection Services

part.name: objective
part.p: Collections and monies received are posted to customer accounts in an accurate and timely manner.

part.name: applicability
part.p: Note: The following controls apply to debt collection service providers only. Add this section if it is relevant to the service provided to the FIs.

part.name: item
part.p: Debt collection procedures are documented to guide personnel in the debt collection process.

part.name: item
part.p: Debt collection instructions are scanned into a document imaging application for archiving and retrieval.

part.name: item
part.p: The outstanding amounts in debt collection instructions are recorded and reconciled to the collected amounts before posting to the FIs’ accounts.

part.name: item
part.p: The debt collection report is reviewed by the checker before the posting is approved.

part.name: item
part.p: The identities of the maker and checker are recorded for accountability.

control.title: Sample Controls for Physical and Electronic Statement Printing Services

prop.name: service-type
prop.value: Physical and Electronic Statement Printing Services

part.name: objective
part.p: Customer Statements are printed accurately and sent timely to FIs’ customers.

part.name: applicability
part.p: Note: The following controls apply to Physical and Electronic Statement Printing service providers only. Add this section if it is relevant to the service provided to the FIs.

part.name: item
part.p: Statement printing procedures are documented to guide personnel in the statement printing process.

part.name: item
part.p: A statement schedule outlines when statements are required to be printed and mailed for each customer.

part.name: item
part.p: System reports with batch and hash totals are reconciled to ensure the completeness and accuracy of printed statements.

part.name: item
part.p: The identities of the checker and verifier of system reconciliation reports are recorded for accountability.

part.name: objective
part.p: These controls provide reasonable assurance that the OSP classifies data according to sensitivity, which determines protection requirements, access rights and restrictions, and retention and destruction requirements.

control.title: Data are classified according to sensitivity, which determines protection requirements, access rights and restrictions, and the retention and destruction requirements

part.name: objective
part.p: Data are classified according to sensitivity, which determines protection requirements, access rights and restrictions, and the retention and destruction requirements.

part.name: item
part.p: Policies for data classification, retention and destruction are implemented. Retention is as required by local law (governing the FIs) or as required by the FIs.

part.name: item
part.p: Data held with the OSP (both in physical and electronic forms) are stored in appropriate media where the level of backups is determined based on the classification of data. For information/records held in electronic storage media (including cloud based storage services), the OSP should ensure that appropriate levels of data/record segregation exist to prevent co-mingling of data. Logical segregation is an acceptable form of control to segregate customer information held electronically.

part.name: item
part.p: Procedures on retention of information and data should be implemented. These procedures should clearly state retention guidelines based on the classification of information/data, applicable laws and agreed with the FIs.

part.name: item
part.p: Procedures on destruction of information and data by the OSP should be implemented. These procedures should clearly state the secured destruction process based on the classification of information held. The procedures should be agreed with the FIs.

part.name: item
part.p: For terminated arrangements, the OSP should provide the FIs with the relevant evidence that demonstrates that all forms of data/records/information (both electronic and physical) given to the OSP and sub-contractor (where applicable) have been promptly removed or deleted, destroyed or rendered unusable, unless the OSP or sub-contractor is prohibited from doing so by law.

part.name: item
part.p: Ownership of data, and the roles and responsibilities of the staff managing the data is defined.

part.name: objective
part.p: These controls provide reasonable assurance that physical assets held by the OSP are safeguarded from loss, misappropriation and unauthorised access.

control.title: Physical assets owned by the OSP to deliver the service and/or assets owned by FIs under OSP’s monitoring and controls are safeguarded from loss, misappropriation and unauthorised access

part.name: objective
part.p: Physical assets owned by the OSP to deliver the service and/or assets owned by FIs under OSP’s monitoring and controls are safeguarded from loss, misappropriation and unauthorised access.

part.name: item
part.p: Physical assets owned by OSP to deliver the service and/or assets owned by FIs under OSP's monitoring and control are safeguarded from loss, misappropriation and unauthorised access. Physical access to the operational OSP’s office/facilities is restricted to authorised personnel at all times. The entry to office/ facilities is through an automated proximity access card entry control system.

part.name: item
part.p: Access to offices/ facilities after normal business hours is pre-approved. Access is monitored 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.

part.name: item
part.p: Physical assets (e.g. office equipment, storage media) are tagged and are assigned to custodians. Fixed assets counts are performed every 12 months and movements of assets are tracked and recorded.

part.name: objective
part.p: These controls provide reasonable assurance that OSP’s engagement with FIs and sub-contractors handling material outsourcing and FIs’ customer information are properly managed.

control.title: Outsourced activities are properly managed and monitored

part.name: objective
part.p: Outsourced activities are properly managed and monitored.

part.name: item
part.p: A governance framework supported by policies, procedures, guidelines and standards is established to manage and deliver its services.

part.name: item
part.p: Due diligence and risk assessments of sub-contractors providing sub-contracted services are performed at least annually or at a frequency agreed with the FIs. The due diligence includes the review of independent audit/expert assessment reports.

part.name: item
part.p: The governance procedures include regular training for employees and sub-contractors/ third parties to ensure that employees and sub-contractors/ third parties are aware of relevant regulatory requirements (e.g. anti-bribery and banking secrecy).

part.name: item
part.p: SLAs with FIs and sub-contractors clearly define performance monitoring (e.g. performance measures and indicators such as system uptime and turnaround time for document processing) and reporting requirements. Achievements of agreed key performance indicators (“KPIs”) and key risk indicators (“KRIs”) are tracked and monitored.

part.name: item
part.p: Procedures are established for service recovery and reporting of lapses relating to the agreed service standards, including processes ensuring regular exchange of information and communication of critical issues.

part.name: item
part.p: The OSP arranges regular meetings with FI clients and sub-contractors/ third parties to discuss performance and service delivery outcomes. Corrective actions and plans are prepared and agreed with FI clients and sub- contractors to address performance and service delivery gaps.

part.name: objective
part.p: These controls provide reasonable assurance that business continuity plans are documented, approved, tested and maintained.

control.title: Business Continuity Plan (BCP) is documented, approved, tested and maintained

part.name: objective
part.p: Business Continuity Plan (BCP) is documented, approved, tested and maintained.

part.name: statement
part.p: Business Continuity Management (BCM) refers to a set of practices that includes putting in place policies, standards, processes, and measures to provide for continuous functioning of the organisation during operational disruptions.

part.name: item
part.p: A business continuity plan is established and maintained based on business, operational and information technology needs of FI.

part.name: item
part.p: The OSP could consider including the below areas within their BCP:

part.name: item
part.p: critical business functions segregation – separate critical business functions into different zones to mitigate the risk of losing multiple critical business functions, and the critical business services that they support, from a wide area disruption;

part.name: item
part.p: split team and back-up team arrangements – deploying critical personnel across different zones, or establish reserve team arrangements to eliminate the dependency on a single labour pool;

part.name: item
part.p: cross-training – identify critical skills or roles, and develop cross-training programs to build versatility for key personnel involved in these roles;

part.name: item
part.p: cross-border support – activate cross-border support as a contingency during disruptions; or

part.name: item
part.p: contingency plan to support subcontracted critical business functions, in the event that the subcontractor is unavailable.

part.name: item
part.p: OSP should have clearly defined criteria for BCP activation when a critical business service encounters partial disruption (including intermittent or reduced performance that is not tantamount to a complete unavailability of service). This will guide the OSP in activating its BCP in a timely and decisive manner before the service degradation worsens to the point that it results in severe impact.

part.name: item
part.p: OSP should notify the FIs of any substantial changes in the OSPs’ BCP plans and of any adverse development that could substantially impact the services provided to the FIs.

part.name: item
part.p: Roles and responsibilities of relevant personnel in the business continuity process should be included in the plan.

part.name: item
part.p: Business continuity policy, plan and procedures, including the relevant training programmes for staff, activation and escalation process, are regularly reviewed and updated based on the changes in the OSP’s operational environment and the threat landscape. FIs should also be permitted to participate in BCP tests as appropriate.

part.name: item
part.p: Critical business services and functions of the OSP that support the service should have their respective RTOs defined. Such services / functions and their defined RTOs are reviewed at least annually, or whenever there are material changes that affect them.

part.name: item
part.p: Comprehensive testing of BCM should be conducted on a regular basis, to ensure that the OSP's business continuity processes are robust and enable them to continue the delivery of critical business services in a timely and reliable manner following a disruption. The test objectives, scope and defined frequency of these tests should be commensurate with the criticality of the business services and functions.

part.name: item
part.p: All BCP test records, clearly indicating details, such as the test objectives, scope, scenario design, participants involved, results and follow-ups for each test should be clearly documented.
Gaps and weaknesses identified from the OSP's business continuity testing should be addressed and reported to the senior management.

part.name: item
part.p: Formal process to track, assign ownership and follow up on the remedial actions identified in each test is established. The effectiveness of the remediation measures undertaken should also be validated at subsequent tests to ensure proper implementation.
